subject: Clarify point-of-capture definition and options for retroactive evidence
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fincloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 Type II — question on point-of-capture for audit period (Apr 1 2027 - Mar 31 2028)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this — a couple of follow-ups from our SOC 2 Type II review for FinCloud. The auditor team needs clarity on two closely related items for the period Apr 1, 2027 — Mar 31, 2028:

1) Point-of-capture definition: For activity captured at a period boundary (e.g., 00:00 UTC on Mar 31), do you treat requests that were still "in-flight" but committed after the boundary as within the period, or only those whose final persistence occurred before the cutoff? Please be explicit about the cutoff semantics you used for the report.

2) Retroactive evidence for a restart event: We noted an operational incident on Mar 30 where a subset of inference nodes restarted and a small percentage of request logs were flagged as missing in the hot index. Can Redwood supply reconstructed request evidence (export), or would you issue a bridge letter describing the reconstruction method and limitations? If reconstruction is possible, what artifacts can you provide and what is the expected turnaround?

The auditor team has requested an initial answer within 48 hours if possible.

Appreciate your help — Laura
Laura Chen
Security Engineer, FinCloud Systems
laura.chen@fincloud.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fincloud.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II — question on point-of-capture for audit period (Apr 1 2027 - Mar 31 2028)

Thanks Laura — looping in Dev and Marissa to confirm the technical capture semantics and whether we can produce reconstructed exports for the Mar 30 incident. Quick context for the team: the auditor wants to know how we determine inclusion at period cutoffs (as-of vs through) and whether we can provide retroactive evidence for requests that appear missing in the hot index after the node restarts.

Dev — can you confirm:
- Exactly how our point-of-capture is defined for the Type II report (do we use commit timestamp/persistence write as the authoritative moment?),
- Retention tiers and whether cold storage indices can be used to reconstruct missing entries, and
- Estimated ETA to produce a reconstructed export + supporting manifest if we commit to doing so.

Marissa — if recon is viable, we may need an official bridge letter to document the method and limitations; any guidance on legal/CS signoff cadence?

Laura — we'll aim to get you a consolidated reply within 48 business hours.

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fincloud.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II — question on point-of-capture for audit period (Apr 1 2027 - Mar 31 2028)

Hi all — technical details below; TL;DR: our report uses persistence (commit) timestamp as the point-of-capture; we can reconstruct most missing request records from cold-store artifacts but it requires a short backfill process and a bridge letter to document reconstruction limitations.

1) Point-of-capture semantics
- Authoritative moment: commit_persist_ts (the timestamp written when the write is durably acknowledged to storage). For the Type II report we consider an event included in the period if commit_persist_ts < cutoff (cutoff = 2028-03-31T00:00:00Z for your audit).
- Rationale: this aligns with verification of durable state (DB snapshots, object store manifests) rather than ephemeral in-memory processing.

2) What happened on Mar 30 incident
- During the rolling restart a small set of inference frontends lost in-memory indexing pointers; those requests were still successfully received and in many cases persisted, but a subset did not make it into our hot search index before rotation. Cold-store (S3) retained raw request archives and write-ahead logs.

3) Reconstruction capabilities and artifacts we can provide
- redwood_log_export_20280330_reconstructed.csv — reconstructed request rows with best-effort timestamps and a provenance column describing the source (WAL / s3-archive / db-snapshot).
- backup-snapshot-20280330-manifest.json — manifests for object store/dB snapshots we used to reconstruct the export (hashes, offsets).
- bridge_letter_reconstruction_draft.pdf — draft language describing methods, assumptions, and known gaps for auditor review.

4) Limitations and quality notes
- Reconstructed timestamps are derived from write-ahead-log offsets and may have +/- 1-5 second uncertainty in edge cases; we annotate each row accordingly.
- We cannot retroactively reconstruct payloads for any requests that were dropped before persist; such rows will be absent and enumerated in the manifest.

5) ETA and next steps
- If you want the reconstructed export + manifest: estimated delivery 3 business days (work includes rehydration of cold archives, cross-checking against DB snapshot, and manifest generation).
- Bridge letter draft: 1 business day (we can provide a signed PDF after legal/CS sign-off).
- Delivery method: secure Drive link + audit-only DocuSign for bridge letter if signature required.

Proposed approach: produce the export and manifest, simultaneously draft the bridge letter; deliver everything together so auditors have both artifacts and explanatory language.

If that works I will start the cold rehydration job and allocate the SRE runbook for verification.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@fincloud.com>, BrightLine Audit Team <audit@brightline-audit.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC2 Type II — question on point-of-capture for audit period (Apr 1 2027 - Mar 31 2028) — consolidated reply and artifacts plan

Hi Laura / BrightLine team — thanks for raising this. Below is a consolidated answer and our proposed delivery plan.

- Point-of-capture: Redwood uses the commit_persist_ts (the durable write acknowledgement) as the authoritative inclusion moment for the SOC 2 Type II report. Events with commit_persist_ts strictly before 2028-03-31T00:00:00Z are treated as within the audit period; events that committed at or after the cutoff are excluded.

- Mar 30 restart: as Dev explains, the restart caused incomplete indexing in the hot search layer, but cold storage and WAL artifacts preserved the majority of persisted requests.

- What we will deliver: 
  1) redwood_log_export_20280330_reconstructed.csv — a best-effort reconstruction of persisted requests for 2028-03-30 with provenance and timestamp uncertainty annotations.
  2) backup-snapshot-20280330-manifest.json — manifests and hashes for the snapshots/WALs used during reconstruction.
  3) bridge_letter_reconstruction_draft.pdf — draft bridge letter describing methodology, assumptions, and limitations.

- Timeline: we will deliver the reconstructed export and manifest in 3 business days from today (by 2028-06-23 COB PT). The bridge letter draft will be provided within 1 business day for review, with a signed copy available within 2 business days pending legal sign-off.

- Delivery and access: artifacts will be uploaded to a secure audit Drive folder and we will provide time-limited links; if you require a signed bridge letter we will route it via DocuSign. Links and the Drive manifest will be included in the delivery email.

Please let us know if you want us to proceed with the reconstruction now. Once you confirm, Dev will start the cold rehydration job and we'll begin drafting the letter.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Liaison, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

— on behalf of Dev Patel (SRE) and Marissa Cole (Head of Trust)

Attachments: redwood_log_export_20280330_reconstructed.csv (pending generation), backup-snapshot-20280330-manifest.json (pending), bridge_letter_reconstruction_draft.pdf (attached for initial review)
